title: Prediction of long-term psychosocial burden and relevant participation restrictions among breast cancer patients undergoing rehabilitation: Development of a prediction model
summary:
After being diagnosed with breast cancer, many women continue to suffer from physical and psychological distress even after completing their medical treatment. Fatigue, depressive symptoms or limitations in daily life often affect their quality of life and make it difficult to return to work and social life.
Oncological rehabilitation is designed to help patients to improve their health and participation in society. 

In a previous project, data from 437 breast cancer patients who had taken part in a rehabilitation right after hospital stay were analysed. Further analysis revealed that there are different groups with varying severity of symptoms. Particularly striking was a group of breast cancer rehabilitation patients with persistently high physical and psychological distress. Even one year after rehabilitation, these patients more frequently experienced difficulties returning to work and suffered more often from depressive symptoms.

The ongoing project builds on these findings. The aim is to develop a simple screening tool to identify highly distressed breast cancer patients at an early stage, either before or at the very beginning of rehabilitation. This should enable those affected to receive more targeted support in the future and be provided with suitable support services more quickly. The screening tool will then be evaluated in everyday rehabilitation practice to assess its comprehensibility and practical feasibility.

interventions.name:
30 women participating in breast cancer rehabilitation are interviewed using a newly developed screening tool at the start of their rehabilitation programme. In addition, the participants are given a questionnaire covering socio-demographic details, health status and comorbidities.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The study includes women aged 18 to 65 who are participating in a breast cancer rehabilitation programme at the Asklepios Nordseeklinik Westerland.
Exclusion criteria:
Rehabilitation patients without a confirmed diagnosis of breast cancer and who have insufficient knowledge of German will be excluded from the study. In addition, not consenting to take part in the study is an exclusion criterion.
